episodes.199530: An isolated supercell thunderstorm produced marginally severe hail over a small portion of central Virginia.
episodes.199539: Light showers in a very strong background wind field resulted in sporadic borderline storm-force wind gusts during the afternoon hours.
episodes.199681: Upper-level trough with enhanced flow and upper-level divergence in the wake of a surface cold front passage allowed for breezy to gusty winds to begin during the late morning and early afternoon hours of April 15, 2025. Ample moisture with sufficient lift and marginal instability allowed for numerous showers to form, producing gusty winds. As showers moved further south and east, elevated surface-based instability allowed for some thunderstorms to form, with damaging winds during the late afternoon hours. Shower coverage began to wane later in the day as the best forcing and upper-level flow shifted east of the region, with widespread damage across Centre and Dauphin Counties and isolated pockets of damage across eastern Pennsylvania.
episodes.200879: A strong cold front crossed the area producing scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms. The front moved into an environment that had limited instability yet strong winds aloft. The lower atmosphere was also supportive of mixing down strong damaging wind gusts to the surface as was the case with a few of the showers and thunderstorms crossing the Southern Tier of NY.
episodes.201416: Storms developed along and in advance of a cold front. Some of these storms became strong enough to produce damaging winds and hail.
episodes.201424: A southeastward moving cold front encountered marginal instability in southwest Virginia, producing an isolated report of severe straight line wind damage in Wise.
episodes.201621: In the midst of a passing low pressure system, strong thunderstorms crossed into southwest Virginia on the evening of April 14th. These storms were notorious for producing very large hail as they traveled through the Ohio Valley and into West Virginia throughout the afternoon, and this bled into Buchanan County with a single observance of ping pong sized hail occurring in Hurley. Activity then quickly pressed eastward into central Virginia for the remainder of the evening.
episodes.201781: A lone storm was able to produce 1 inch hail as it tracked through Ellis County during the early morning hours on April 15th.
episodes.201824: A non-severe thunderstorm moved across northern Chenango County in Central New York during the late evening hours. A house was struck by lightning and was deemed to be a total loss after a fire.
episodes.202062: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and moved across eastern Pennsylvania and northwestern New Jersey in response to a closed low north of our region.
episodes.202063: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed and moved across eastern Pennsylvania and northwestern New Jersey in response to a closed low north of our region.
episodes.202128: A digging low pressure system and its attendant frontal boundary served up strong thunderstorms across the state of West Virginia on the afternoon of April 14th. Storms first formed over the lower Ohio Valley during the late morning hours and then tracked into West Virginia for the afternoon and evening hours. Damaging winds and large hail were noted within the strongest storms. A swath of large hail between 1.5 to 2.25 inches fell over Cabell County and across the Kanawha Valley into the foothills of the Appalachian mountains. Tree and power line damage was also observed within the strongest storms that afternoon before activity quickly dashed east of the mountains by that evening.
episodes.202190: Storms developed along and in advance of a cold front. Some of these storms became strong enough to produce damaging winds and hail.
episodes.202269: A deepening low pressure passing north of Lake Superior caused winds to gust to storm force on the 15th.
episodes.202278: A large area of low pressure (992 mb) moved across the Great Lakes on April 14. Isolated storms tracked across West Virginia and into Virginia during the evening. One of these storms produced large hail and damaging winds as it moved across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.202279: A large area of low pressure (992 mb) moved across the Great Lakes on April 14. Isolated storms tracked across West Virginia and into Virginia during the evening. One of these storms produced gusty winds as it moved across the Chesapeake Bay overnight.
episodes.202296: A cold front moved across the local waters on April 15. An isolated storm produced gusty winds across the Maryland coastal waters along the cold front. Winds became elevated behind the front across the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.206835: A line of storms developed across Kentucky ahead of a cold front that began pushing into the state from the west during the afternoon hours on the 14th. As it continued to traverse the state and move into eastern Kentucky, the line of storms resulted in numerous instances of severe weather, including hail and damaging winds. The system them exited overnight, with storms and instances of severe weather ending just after midnight on the 15th in Harlan County.
